adapter_lora_config_reconstructed.config_source: RECONSTRUCTED — adapter_config.json was MISSING from saved retry-3 adapter dir; r/alpha/target_modules derived from spec doc + safetensors tensor shape inspection (lora_A.weight = [64, 8192], lora_B.weight = [3072, 64])

axis_eval_set_construction: 5-axis taxonomy from bench/zeta_likert/v1_frozen.json (daily/emotion/task/roleplay/meta) × 20 base prompts × 5 axis-conditioning prefixes per prompt = 100 prompts; balanced 20-per-axis; 20 'native_axis == conditioned_axis' true-positives + 80 cross-axis prompts
methodology: Forward each prompt through (a) Llama-3.2-3B base with LoRA adapter DISABLED (PeftModel.disable_adapter context), (b) same model with adapter ENABLED. Capture last-layer last-token hidden state per pass. Per axis A, compute v_base[A] = mean of base hidden states over A's 20 prompts and v_lora[A] = same for LoRA. axis_preservation[A] = cosine_similarity(v_base[A], v_lora[A]). mean_preservation_score = mean over 5 axes.

axis_discrimination.interpretation: Both base AND LoRA show very high pairwise similarity across axes (>0.99) — the 5 axis-mean vectors are nearly collinear in either model. LoRA does NOT degrade axis discrimination meaningfully; absolute discrimination delta is -0.08 percentage points. This means the FAIL on preservation is NOT because LoRA collapsed axes onto each other — it's because LoRA shifted ALL axes ~equally in representation space.

f_pa_retrain_v2_4_thresholds_per_spec.verdict_reason: mean 0.7871 < 0.85 FAIL threshold; ALL 5 individual axis scores also < 0.85 PARTIAL threshold

closes_reason: F4 = FAIL means 1 of 5 gates does NOT pass; lane is now F1=PASS, F2=PASS, F3=PASS, F4=FAIL, F5=PASS — overall MIXED, not fully green
honest_c3: anima_axis_preservation as defined in this BG (cosine similarity between base axis-mean hidden state and post-LoRA axis-mean hidden state, last-layer last-token) is an ANIMA-INTERNAL HEURISTIC, not an industry-standard metric — the 0.95/0.85 thresholds are spec-prescribed and not externally calibrated. A score of 0.7871 indicates substantial representation shift but does NOT directly imply behavioral degradation; F1/F2/F3/F5 (loss convergence, no-drop, parity, etc.) are the ultimate behavioral signals and they all PASS_TRUE per the eval-rerun spec citation.

100 prompts (20 per axis) is the spec-prescribed N; with hidden-dim 3072 (Llama-3.2-3B) and 20 samples per axis-mean, the axis-mean variance is meaningful but a 95% CI on cosine sim would still be ~±0.02-0.04 — so the FAIL verdict is robust against stderr; even pessimistic upper-CI on individual axes would still be <0.85 PARTIAL boundary.

adapter_config.json was MISSING from the saved retry-3 adapter checkpoint dir (only adapter_model.safetensors present). I RECONSTRUCTED the config from (a) spec doc declaring r=64 alpha=64 dropout=0.05, (b) tensor shape inspection deriving 7 target_modules q/k/v/o + gate/up/down. If the actual training-time config differed (e.g. magnitude_vector or DoRA option set), the reconstructed config could be subtly wrong and the LoRA forward pass could produce slightly different activations. Given the smoke-test forward pass succeeded without shape errors and PEFT loaded all 392 lora_A/B tensors cleanly, gross misconfiguration is ruled out.

Methodology uses last-layer last-token hidden state — this is a STANDARD probe for sentence-level representation but it conflates 'axis identity' with 'axis-conditioning prefix token influence'. A more rigorous metric would (a) probe multiple layers and (b) use a held-out classifier trained on base axes to test whether LoRA preserves axis-classifier accuracy. Deferred for cost (this BG is $0 ubu1, ~8s wall).

The axis_discrimination side-channel finding (mean_pairwise_cos_base=0.9940, mean_pairwise_cos_lora=0.9932) suggests that even Llama-3.2-3B base CANNOT strongly discriminate between the 5 anima axes at this representation level — the axis-mean vectors are nearly collinear (>0.99 cosine) regardless of adapter. This is a STRONG caveat: 'preservation of a near-degenerate signal' may not be meaningful, since there isn't much axis structure in base Llama to begin with for KO conversational prompts. The FAIL verdict therefore says 'LoRA shifted the representation' more than 'LoRA broke axis-conditioning' (because there is no clear baseline axis-conditioning to break).

Forward path used PeftModel.disable_adapter() context for base pass + default ENABLED for LoRA pass — this is functionally equivalent to loading two models but ~half the GPU memory cost. The FIRST attempt (which OOMed at 11GB / 12GB RTX 5070 capacity) used two separate model loads and crashed at the second .to(DEVICE) — the disable_adapter approach succeeded in 8s wall.

ubu1 RTX 5070 + bf16 + Llama-3.2-3B = 6.5GB model + ~3GB activations for max_length=512 = ~9.5GB total — within 12GB budget. Per-prompt forward latency averaged ~0.06s including tokenization, hidden state extraction, and CPU offload. 200 forwards (100 base + 100 LoRA) in 8s = ~25 prompts/sec.

Verdict NEGATIVE-INFORMATIVE: F-PA-RETRAIN-v2-4 = FAIL closes the 'F4 DEFERRED' status from the eval-rerun verdict but does NOT achieve the all-green 1/2/3/4/5 PASS for Path A retry-3 lane. Lane status is now F1=PASS F2=PASS F3=PASS F4=FAIL F5=PASS — 4-of-5 PASS. Whether to treat this as 'lane PASS with axis caveat' or 'lane FAIL' is a downstream policy decision (per spec the gates are AND-ed by default = lane FAIL on F4=FAIL).

Cost was $0 actual (ubu1 free local GPU) vs ~$0.30-0.60 estimated had this run on H100. wall_time 8s actual vs 1-2h spec estimate is 99.7% under — primarily because (a) ubu1 5070 has bf16 + tensor-core acceleration sufficient for 3B-param model + 100 prompts and (b) hidden-state extraction is much cheaper than text generation.
